title: control-plane: emit structured incident annotations for status component mapping
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: Control plane services now emit structured incident annotations (redacted/safe) to improve status page component mapping accuracy and reduce manual interpretation during incidents.
body:
## Context
As part of Status page transparency upgrades (ENG-4821), we need a consistent, machine-readable way for control plane services to describe what customer-facing surface area is likely impacted (region, route family, deployment mode, etc.). Today, oncall often stitches this together from dashboards/logs and we frequently over-broadcast impact (e.g., marking "API" degraded when it’s streaming-only).

This PR adds a small schema + emitters in the control plane to produce structured "incident annotations" that are safe to export to our incident workflow tooling (incident-bot/status tooling) and later map to public status components.

## What this does
- Adds `IncidentAnnotation` schema (JSON payload) with a small set of controlled fields.
- Emits annotations from:
  - `control-plane-gateway` (route + auth tier + request class)
  - `capacity-scheduler` (capacity/routing constraints; region + pool)
  - `model-registry` (model family/version rollouts; serving mode)
- Adds log + metric plumbing:
  - Structured log event `incident.annotation`
  - Counter `incident_annotations_emitted_total{service,category}`
- Includes examples + guidance in code comments for future emitters.

## Schema (v1)
`IncidentAnnotation` is intended to be customer-safe *by construction*:
- No customer identifiers
- No prompt/content
- No provider/contractual details
- No vuln-like detail (per external comms policy)

Fields:
- `schema_version`: "1"
- `timestamp_ms`: unix ms
- `service`: emitting service name
- `category`: one of `routing_capacity | api_gateway | rollout | auth | networking | dependency`
- `scope.deployment_mode`: `hosted | dedicated | private`
- `scope.region`: e.g. `us-east | us-west | eu-west | unknown`
- `scope.routes`: array of route families (controlled values): `chat_completions | completions | embeddings | rerank | streaming`
- `scope.model_families`: array (e.g., `llama3 | mistral | qwen | unknown`)
- `suspected_impact`: `errors | increased_latency | timeouts | rate_limits | degraded_quality | unknown`
- `confidence`: `low | medium | high`
- `related_incident_id`: optional internal incident id (not public)
- `links`: optional array of runbook/dashboard links (internal only)

## Examples
1) Streaming-only disconnect spike in us-east:
`{"schema_version":"1","timestamp_ms":1720034105123,"service":"control-plane-gateway","category":"api_gateway","scope":{"deployment_mode":"hosted","region":"us-east","routes":["streaming"],"model_families":["unknown"]},"suspected_impact":"errors","confidence":"high"}`

2) Capacity constraint on dedicated pool in eu-west affecting embeddings/rerank:
`{"schema_version":"1","timestamp_ms":1720035900123,"service":"capacity-scheduler","category":"routing_capacity","scope":{"deployment_mode":"dedicated","region":"eu-west","routes":["embeddings","rerank"],"model_families":["unknown"]},"suspected_impact":"rate_limits","confidence":"medium"}`

## How this will be used
- Incident-bot will ingest/attach these annotations to an incident timeline event stream.
- Status page component selection helper (ENG-4828) can map `scope.*` fields into a suggested component set (e.g., `Hosted API > Streaming (us-east)` vs global `Hosted API`).
- The annotations also provide an audit trail for why we marked a particular component as impacted.

## Testing
- Unit tests validate schema versioning + allowed enums.
- Golden tests for each emitter (ensures fields stay within allowed set).
- Manual sanity: ran `control-plane-gateway` locally and verified structured log events appear and metrics increment.

## Rollout / risk
- Emitters are behind feature flag `incident_annotations.enabled` (default off).
- Flag will be enabled in `us-east` only as part of the incident-bot canary (ENG-4825).
- If anything goes wrong, disabling the flag returns us to current behavior (no functional impact).

## Notes on disclosure
Per Security review, we intentionally avoid emitting:
- request ids / trace ids that could be customer-correlated
- customer org ids
- exact model ids that may reveal customer-pinned variants
- dependency vendor names

Follow-ups
- Add emitter in `private-control-plane` once schema is validated in hosted + dedicated.
- Wire annotations into the incident timeline store (owned by incident-bot changes in PR #48225 / incident-bot PRs).
commits: control-plane: add incident annotation schema + validators
gateway: emit incident.annotation for route family spikes
scheduler: emit capacity/rate-limit annotations with region + pool scope
model-registry: emit rollout-related annotations (model family + mode)
obs: add metric + structured logging helpers; golden tests
review_conversation:
Miles Thornton (review): This is the missing piece for component mapping. A few nits: (1) can we make `scope.routes` a controlled enum instead of free-form strings? (2) I want a hard guardrail that we never emit org/customer identifiers (even accidentally).

Ethan Park (author): Good call. Updated `routes` to a strict enum with validator + golden tests; also added a `disallowed_keys` check in `validate.ts` (fails fast if payload includes `customer_id`, `org_id`, `account_id`, `email`, `request_id`, `trace_id`).

Christine Wong (review): For status components, region scoping is critical. In a few places you emit `region: "unknown"` even though we have region in context. Can we plumb region from the gateway request context and the scheduler pool metadata?

Ethan Park (author): Fixed both. Gateway now reads `ctx.region` from the existing routing context. Scheduler uses `pool.region` (was previously only in logs). Golden tests updated.

Aisha Bello (review): +1. Please add a metric label for `category` so we can dashboard emitted volume by category and service.

Ethan Park (author): Added `incident_annotations_emitted_total{service,category}` and updated the helper to enforce bounded cardinality.

Marcus Lin (security review): Thanks for keeping this customer-safe. Two requests: remove `links` by default (internal URLs sometimes include sensitive query params), and add docstring guidance that dependency vendor names must not be included.

Ethan Park (author): Done. `links` is now only allowed for a fixed allowlist of runbook slugs (no raw URLs) and is optional; also added explicit comments + validation rejecting `vendor`, `provider`, `cve`, and `exploit` fields.

Miles Thornton (review): Re-ran tests, looks good. Approving.

Christine Wong (review): Approving; this will reduce the back-and-forth during incidents.

Aisha Bello (review): Approved.

Marcus Lin (review): Approved from Security side (schema v1).
merge_outcome: Merged via squash merge into main
